name: Hermes

seo.title: Hermes Galapagos Catamaran: Luxury Cruise | James Wild & Co
seo.description: Hermes by Via Natura: a 50-metre motor catamaran built in 2025 for 20 guests in 12 suites, each with a balcony and jacuzzi. 2026 and 2027 rates and charter.

tagline: Twelve suites for 20 guests, each with a private balcony and jacuzzi, and 20 crew.
answer: Hermes is a 50-metre (164 ft) motor catamaran that Via Natura built in 2025 and owns. She carries 20 guests in 12 suites, every one with a private balcony and an ocean-view jacuzzi, and 20 crew, including two butlers, a cruise director and two naturalist guides. Via Natura sells her by the suite on routes of 3 to 14 nights, or as a full charter. 2026 fares start at US$7,095 per person for 3 nights. She suits couples and private groups who want a spa, butler service and suite-only living in the islands.

overview: Hermes is a motor catamaran that Via Natura, a Galapagos and Andes operator, built in 2025 and owns outright. She is 50 metres long with a 14-metre beam and carries 20 guests. Via Natura calls her an ultra-luxury mega catamaran and says she has more than 730 square metres of social areas.

All 12 suites have a private balcony, a private ocean-view jacuzzi, motorised blackout curtains, a Bluetooth sound system and a stocked minibar included in the fare. The Owner Suite (72 sq m) has two jacuzzis; the nine King/Twin Suites (35 sq m) and the Owner Suite have walk-in closets; two Single Suites (22 sq m) are sold to solo travellers. On board are the Paradiso restaurant, Sole e Luna for dining outdoors, the Aperitivo Lounge bar, a library, a spa with a hammam and massage room, a gym, an observation deck and a sun deck with an outdoor jacuzzi.

Via Natura publishes four itineraries, A and B of 4 nights and C and D of 3 nights, and combines them into cruises of 6 to 14 nights. The island routes for each letter appear only on Via Natura's itinerary maps, not as text. One published 9-day programme pairs a 7-night cruise from Baltra with nights at Casa Gangotena in Quito.
why: Twenty crew for twenty guests, two butlers who each look after one passenger deck, and two naturalist guides with no more than ten guests each. Every suite has its own balcony and jacuzzi.

Via Natura says she was the first small ship in the Galapagos with a full-service spa, and she has a hammam. She can be chartered whole for up to 20 guests, with published charter rates for 2026 and 2027.

itineraries.name: Hermes with Quito: 9-day programme, 7 nights aboard
itineraries.direction: Quito to Baltra, then back to Quito

days.title: Arrive in Quito
days.summary: Met at the airport and driven to Casa Gangotena in Quito's old town for the night.

days.title: Fly to Baltra and the Santa Cruz highlands
days.summary: Help with check-in in Quito, then the flight to Baltra. Afternoon in the Santa Cruz highlands for giant tortoises, lava tunnels, the tortoise breeding centre and Darwin's finches. First night aboard.

days.title: Rabida and Bartolome
days.summary: Red sand beach and lagoon on Rabida with flamingos and marine iguanas, then Bartolome for Pinnacle Rock, its lunar landscape and penguins.

days.title: South Plaza and Santa Fe
days.summary: Via Natura's heading names South Plaza and Santa Fe, but the text under it repeats the Rabida and Bartolome visits of day 3. Indicative: James confirms the day's sites with Via Natura.

days.title: San Cristobal and Santa Fe
days.summary: Morning on San Cristobal and afternoon at Santa Fe, as Via Natura's heading gives it, with no further detail; Santa Fe also appears under day 4. Indicative: James confirms the order with Via Natura.

days.title: Isla Lobos and Cerro Tijeretas
days.summary: Morning at Isla Lobos off San Cristobal, afternoon at the Interpretation Center and Cerro Tijeretas (Frigatebird Hill).

days.title: Gardner Bay and Punta Suarez
days.summary: Morning at Gardner Bay and afternoon at Punta Suarez on Espanola.

days.title: Punta Cormorant and Post Office Bay
days.summary: Morning at Punta Cormorant and afternoon at the barrel post office in Post Office Bay. Last night aboard.

days.title: Back to Quito
days.summary: Disembark and fly back to Quito, with a private transfer to Casa Gangotena. The disembarkation port is not published.

pricesNote: Per person, cruise only, in US dollars, as Via Natura publishes them on vianatura.com (read 2 Nov 2026). The same per-person fare applies in a double suite or a Single Suite. Peak season adds 10%; Via Natura does not publish the peak dates. A solo traveller in a King/Twin Suite paid a 75% single supplement in 2026; the 2027 supplement is not published. The required flights to the Galapagos, booked through Via Natura, are US$600 economy or US$685 premium economy round trip from Quito or Guayaquil. The full charter is for up to 20 guests.

faqs: How much does a Hermes cruise cost?

For 2026 Via Natura publishes US$7,095 per person for 3 nights, US$9,250 for 4 nights and US$14,495 for 7 nights. 2027 fares run from US$7,750 for 3 nights to US$29,795 for 14 nights. Peak season adds 10%, and the Galapagos flights (from US$600) are extra; the park fee is included.
How many guests does Hermes carry?
Twenty, in 12 suites, with 20 crew, including two butlers, a cruise director and two naturalist guides.
The Owner Suite is 72 sq m with two jacuzzis, the nine King/Twin Suites are 35 sq m and the two Single Suites are 22 sq m. Every suite has a private balcony and a private jacuzzi.
Can I charter the whole boat?
Yes. Via Natura publishes full-charter rates for up to 20 guests: from US$134,805 for 3 nights to US$520,505 for 14 nights in 2026, and from US$147,250 to US$566,195 in 2027.

Four routes: A and B of 4 nights, C and D of 3 nights, combined into cruises of 6 to 14 nights. A published 9-day programme flies to Baltra and visits Santa Cruz, Rabida, Bartolome, San Cristobal, Espanola and Floreana.
There are two Single Suites at the standard per-person fare. A solo traveller in a King/Twin Suite paid a 75% supplement in 2026; the 2027 figure is not published.
Via Natura gives 15% off for a child under 12 sharing with two adults, outside peak season and promotions. It does not publish a minimum age.

Meals, selected wines, beer and cocktails, the minibar, butler service, guided excursions, snorkel gear, kayaks and paddleboards, internet, limited laundry, the park entrance fee and the transit card. Flights, gratuities, massages, insurance and a fuel surcharge are extra.

terms: Suites (1 to 4): a 20% non-refundable deposit, and the balance 60 days before departure.
Full charter: a 20% deposit, 30% at 180 days and 50% at 120 days before departure; cancellation inside 120 days forfeits 100%.
Groups and charters follow longer payment schedules, which James confirms with Via Natura.
